So, with the brevity of this article, and its premise, I found coming with a crosslink proposal a little difficult. Then I reread the bit at the bottom about federal agents, and remembered that we have an entire GoI that is federal agents: the UIU. However, this is not a UIU article, so the link should be inline so as to keep the connection as noninvasive as possible. As such, I am proposing the following edits:

Changing this:

Following repeated use of SCP-969, several federal vehicles were seen approaching Site-██. Security forces were deployed and all federal agents were successfully captured. When interviewed, the agents claimed that they had received orders to arrest several substance abusers at the Site-██ location. So far the source of the orders has not been identified. Agents were administered a Class-A amnesiac and returned to ███ Headquarters.

To this:

Following repeated use of SCP-969, several federal vehicles were seen approaching Site-██. Security forces were deployed and all federal agents were successfully captured. When interviewed, the agents claimed that they had received orders to arrest several substance abusers at the Site-██ location. So far the source of the orders has not been identified. Agents were administered a Class-A amnesiac and returned to ███ Headquarters.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.content:encoded:
SCP-969's packaging claims that approximately 19% of SCP-969 is composed of an unknown isomer labelled ████.

From Wikipedia:

In chemistry, isomers … are compounds with the same molecular formula but different structural formulas.

So you can't say something is simply "made of isomers", it has to be isomers of something. I think the label from the photo must mean that 1% of the repellent is isomers of the main active ingredient.

Also, shouldn't the SCP do something if you use it in a manner against federal regulations for insect repellents? Like cause you to be arrested and convicted of a crime?
